summary: YoY Upload Modal Bug Investigation (Iter 333) - UNABLE TO REPRODUCE. Tested manual entry, CSV file upload, and save functionality - all working correctly. The modal opens, parses files, and saves data to backend successfully. The user's issue 'dosya yüklüyorum kayıt et diyorum ama kayıt etmiyor' (I upload a file and click save but it doesn't save) could NOT be reproduced with standard CSV format.
action_items: INVESTIGATE USER'S FILE FORMAT: The most likely root cause is that the user's file format is not being parsed correctly. The parser requires: (1) A month column with recognizable patterns like '2024-01', 'Jan 2025', 'Ocak', etc. (2) A revenue column with numeric values > 100. If the user's Excel/PDF/Image has different column names or formats, the parser returns 0 entries and the Save button becomes disabled.

ADD BETTER ERROR FEEDBACK: When file parsing returns 0 entries, the warning toast 'Dosyada satır bulunamadı' appears but may be missed by users. Consider adding a more prominent error message in the modal itself.
REQUEST USER'S ACTUAL FILE: To properly diagnose, need the actual file the user is trying to upload to see what format/structure it has.
CHECK CONSOLE LOGS: Ask user to check browser console for any errors during file upload/save.

YoYUploadModal.js line 105-106: Warning toast 'Dosyada satır bulunamadı' is shown when no rows parsed, but users may miss it
yoy_parser.py: Parser is sophisticated but requires specific column formats - may not handle all Turkish Excel formats

possible_root_causes: User's file has non-standard column names that parser doesn't recognize
User's file has revenue values formatted in a way parser can't parse (e.g., Turkish number format with different separators)
User's file is an image/PDF that OCR fails to extract text from
User's file has month names in a format not in the parser's _MONTH_MAP
User may have clicked Save before file finished processing (async upload)
rca_of_the_issue: UNABLE TO REPRODUCE - The YoY Upload Modal is functioning correctly. The Save button correctly disables when no valid rows exist (rows.length === 0 && expenseRows.length === 0). When a valid CSV file is uploaded, it parses correctly and Save works. The user's issue is most likely due to their specific file format not being recognized by the parser. Recommend: (1) Get user's actual file to test, (2) Add more prominent error message when parsing fails, (3) Consider adding file format examples/templates for users.
